title: Bose Brought Back Wired Earbuds After 11 Years. With ANC. For $99.

components.text: Bose Brought Back Wired Earbuds After 11 Years. With ANC. For $99.
The new Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds draw power through USB-C, skip the battery entirely, and cost a third of Bose's wireless flagship.
Bose spent the last decade convincing people they didn't need cables. Now they're selling them again.

The Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds are exactly what the name promises: wired earbuds with active noise cancellation, USB-C connectivity, and no battery to charge. They're priced at $99, available for preorder now, and ship October 15.

This is Bose's first wired earbud in 11 years. The company discontinued its last wired model back in 2015, right as the industry was sprinting toward true wireless everything. The timing of this return isn't random. Multiple reports cite double-digit growth in wired earbud sales through 2025 and into 2026, driven largely by younger buyers who either never lived through the tangled-cable era or don't care.

What makes these interesting isn't nostalgia. It's the engineering. Traditional wired ANC earbuds, like Bose's own QC20 from 2013, needed a bulky battery pack clipped to the cable. These don't. The Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds pull power directly from the USB-C port on your phone, tablet, or laptop. No internal battery. No charging case. No degraded lithium cells three years from now.

The ANC itself uses Bose's QuietControl technology with four microphones, two per earbud, to monitor and cancel ambient sound. You get three modes: Quiet for full ANC, Aware for transparency, and Off for passive listening. All controlled from a button on the cable, not an app, because there is no app.

Audio runs through USB Audio Class 2, which means the earbuds accept lossless input at any sample rate and bit depth, then output at a fixed 24-bit/48kHz. That's higher resolution than most streaming services deliver and better than Bluetooth can manage without codec gymnastics. The wired connection also means zero latency, which matters for video calls, gaming, or any situation where lip sync drift is annoying.

The cable is 4.2 feet long. You get three sizes of silicone eartips, medium and large stability wings, an IPX4 splash rating, and a carry case. It ships in Black, White Smoke, and a limited Dewdrop Mint color.

The obvious compromise is the cable itself. You're tethered to your device, which means no walking away from your desk mid-call and a higher chance of snagging the cord on a door handle. But for $99, you're getting QuietControl ANC in a package that never needs charging and won't be e-waste in five years when the battery dies. That's a third the price of Bose's QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds, which cost $299 and will eventually stop holding a charge.
Bose is betting there's a market for people who'd rather plug in than charge up. Based on the wired earbud sales trajectory, they might be right.
